editorial:
If you love cheesy old horror movies and drive-in nostalgia, this one is a wild ride. The story follows Cecil B. Kaufman, the owner of the last drive-in theater in America, who plans one final marathon night for his loyal fans. He screens four rare films that have never been shown publicly in the country before, each one a loving spoof of a different era of B-movie horror. You get giant monster mayhem, teenage werewolf musicals, a ridiculous Frankenstein twist, and a zombie outbreak that ties everything together. The whole thing feels like a love letter to bad movies, made by people who clearly adore them. It is silly, gross, and packed with energy from start to finish.

The acting is intentionally over the top, which works perfectly for this kind of comedy. The pacing moves fast because you are jumping between four different mini-movies, so nothing drags for long. Some jokes land better than others, and a few scenes push the gross-out humor pretty far, so this is not for everyone. But if you enjoy cult horror, midnight movie vibes, or just want something completely unhinged for a movie night, you will have a blast. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the full experience.
endingExplained: The final segment, Zom-B-Movie, reveals that the drive-in crowd has been infected by a zombie virus spread through contaminated popcorn. As chaos erupts across the theater, Cecil and the survivors fight back while the screen keeps playing. The twist is that the entire marathon was designed to unleash the zombie outbreak on purpose, turning the audience into part of the show. In the end, the drive-in burns down, but the spirit of B-movie horror lives on as the survivors drive off into the night, keeping the cult alive.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves cult horror, B-movies, and midnight movie vibes.
